entities.summary: Charles II, Count of Alençon, was a notable medieval figure in Western Europe, born in 1297 and died in 1346. He played a significant role in the politics of the region, serving as Count of Alençon and Count of Perche from 1325 to 1346. His marriage to Joan of Joigny added to his influence. Charles II was a prominent figure in the history of the region, and his legacy continued to shape the local politics and social dynamics. He was known for his generosity and magnanimity, earning him the nickname the Magnanimous. His reign was marked by several key events, including the establishment of the County of Perche and the strengthening of the County of Alençon. Despite his significant influence, Charles II's legacy was largely overshadowed by the more prominent figures of the time, such as Philip VI of France and the Black Death. Nevertheless, his contributions to the region's history are undeniable, and he remains an important figure in the annals of Western European history. His story is a testament to the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the medieval era.
